claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and biblical scholar, born c. 185 and died c. 253–255 CE.
Origen was head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria and later founded the Christian School of Caesarea.
Origen wrote Contra Celsum at the request of his patron Ambrose, a wealthy Christian who insisted that a Christian needed to write a response to Celsus.
The work was aimed at an audience of people who were interested in Christianity but had not yet made the decision to convert.
Celsus was a pagan philosopher and controversialist who had written a scathing attack on Christianity in his treatise The True Word (Λόγος Ἀληθής, Logos Alēthēs).

Celsus denounced many Christian doctrines as irrational, criticized Christians as uneducated, deluded, unpatriotic, close-minded towards reason, and too accepting of sinners, accused Jesus of performing miracles using black magic, and warned that Christianity was drawing people away from traditional religion.
Contra Celsum is preserved entirely in Greek.
The Contra Celsum is the culmination of the great apologetic movement of the second and third centuries AD, and is for the Greek Church what St Augustine's City of God is for Western Christendom.
It is one of the chief monuments of the coming together of ancient Greek culture and the new faith of the expanding Christian society.
